relationship.statement: For a simple pendulum at small angles, the swing period depends only on string length and gravity, not on the bob's mass. A larger release angle widens the swing and raises peak speed.
assumptions: The string is massless, taut, and rigid, with all mass concentrated at the bob.
Air resistance and friction at the pivot are neglected.
The period formula is exact for small angles and shifts slightly upward at large angles.

quantities.label: String length
quantities.meaning: Distance from the pivot point to the center of the pendulum bob.

quantities.label: Bob mass
quantities.meaning: Mass of the suspended bob, which cancels out of gravitational acceleration.

quantities.label: Release angle
quantities.meaning: Starting angle from vertical when the bob is released from rest.

quantities.label: Gravity
quantities.meaning: Gravitational acceleration pulling the bob downward.

quantities.label: Period
quantities.meaning: Time required to complete one full back-and-forth swing.

quantities.label: Frequency
quantities.meaning: Number of full swings completed each second.

quantities.label: Peak speed
quantities.meaning: Maximum speed of the bob at the lowest point of the swing.

quantities.label: Current angle
quantities.meaning: Instantaneous angle of the pendulum from vertical at time t.

math.code: function compute(inputs, t) { var L = inputs.length; var m = inputs.mass; var g = inputs.gravity; var angle0 = 30; var angle0Rad = angle0 * Math.PI / 180; var period = 2 * Math.PI * Math.sqrt(L / g); var frequency = 1 / period; var maxSpeed = Math.sqrt(2 * g * L * (1 - Math.cos(angle0Rad))); var omega = 2 * Math.PI / period; var phase = omega * t; var angle = angle0 * Math.cos(phase); var angleRad = angle * Math.PI / 180; var bobX = L * Math.sin(angleRad); var bobY = -L * Math.cos(angleRad); var dThetaDt = -angle0Rad * omega * Math.sin(phase); var vx = L * dThetaDt * Math.cos(angleRad); var vy = L * dThetaDt * Math.sin(angleRad); var velScale = 0.25; var velEndX = bobX + velScale * vx; var velEndY = bobY + velScale * vy; var refY = -L; var releaseX = L * Math.sin(angle0Rad); var releaseY = -L * Math.cos(angle0Rad); var bobSize = 0.25 + 0.7 * (m - 0.5) / 4.5; return { period: period, frequency: frequency, maxSpeed: maxSpeed, angle: angle, bobX: bobX, bobY: bobY, refY: refY, releaseX: releaseX, releaseY: releaseY, velEndX: velEndX, velEndY: velEndY, bobSize: bobSize, isShortFast: period < 1.5, isLongSlow: period > 3.0, isNearBottom: Math.abs(angle) < 5 }; }

always: Mass changes size, not swing speed.

cases.text: Short string or strong g: fast swing
Long string or weak g: slow swing
Near bottom: speed is at its peak.

lesson.title: What Changes a Pendulum Swing?
lesson.description: Adjust string length, bob mass, and gravity while watching a pendulum released from 30 degrees. Track its swing angle over time to see what sets the period.
lesson.instructions: Use the sliders to vary string length, bob mass, and gravity, and scrub or play time to inspect the velocity arrow and angle graph.
lesson.goal: Pendulum period increases with string length, decreases with gravity, and does not depend on bob mass.
